Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 4. HOME & EVERYDAY ENVIRONMENT
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Best Present Ever
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.

Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

present — a gift. Example: This present is for you.
gift — something you give to someone. Example: It was a special gift.
best — better than all the others. Example: It was the best present.
better — of higher quality than another. Example: This one is better than that one.
worse — of lower quality than another. Example: The cheap one is worse.
cheap — not expensive. Example: The gift was cheap.
expensive — costing a lot of money. Example: The watch was expensive.
special — not ordinary, important. Example: It was a special day.
wrap — to cover a present in paper. Example: I wrap the gift in blue paper.
surprise — something you did not expect. Example: The party was a surprise.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What is the best present you have received?
• It was cheaper than ...
• It was more expensive than ...
• It was a surprise.
• It is very special.

elements.content: Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
My best present was a bicycle. It was more expensive than my brother's gift, but it was not the most expensive. The surprise was the best part.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: What is the best present you have received? B: A watch. It was expensive but very special. A: Was it a surprise? B: Yes, it was.
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Compare three gifts and choose the best one for a friend.

• What is the best present you have received?
• It was cheaper than ...
• It was more expensive than ...
Writing: Write four to five sentences about "Best Present Ever" using the target grammar.
